content: Ipecacuanha is an over-the-counter (OTC) medication classified as an emetic, which is FDA-approved for the treatment of acute poisoning by inducing vomiting. Common side effects associated with its use include diarrhea, stomach cramps, muscle pain (myalgia), and lethargy. For adults, the FDA-approved indication for Ipecacuanha is to manage acute poisoning by inducing nausea and vomiting. The recommended dosage is to allow 3 or 4 pellets to dissolve in the mouth three times a day until symptoms are alleviated or as directed by a healthcare professional. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of Ipecacuanha in adults, whether supported by guidelines or not. For pediatric patients, Ipecacuanha is also FDA-approved for the treatment of acute poisoning. The dosage is the same as for adults: 3 or 4 pellets dissolved in the mouth three times a day until symptoms resolve or as directed by a healthcare provider. Similar to adults, there is limited information on off-label uses of Ipecacuanha in pediatric populations. There is insufficient information in the drug label regarding contraindications, specific warnings, or postmarketing experiences. However, adverse reactions observed in clinical trials include diarrhea, stomach cramps, myalgia, and lethargy. There is no detailed guidance on drug interactions. Regarding use in specific populations, the FDA advises consulting a healthcare professional if pregnant or breastfeeding. There is no specific guidance on the use of Ipecacuanha during labor and delivery, in pediatric or geriatric populations, or in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no guidance on its use in relation to gender, race, reproductive potential, or immunocompromised patients. Ipecacuanha is administered orally. There is limited information on monitoring requirements, IV compatibility, overdose management, pharmacology, mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology in the drug label. The product is supplied as Ipecacuanha 3X (Ipecac) and contains lactose and sucrose. It should be stored at room temperature. There is no established interaction between alcohol and Ipecacuanha, but patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol use while taking this medication. The brand name for this medication is IPECACUANHA®. There is no detailed information on look-alike drug names, drug shortages, or pricing in the drug label.
